portion_doctrine: Segments 101-110 are a mixed technical transcript spanning 3 distinct domains: (1) Windsurf AI IDE tutorial covering Cascade Memories, multi-file editing, in-line commands, and deployment; (2) OpenAI agents platform documentation covering models, tool-calling, RAG, structured outputs, and Agents SDK; (3) Vibe coding best practices from an independent speaker on AI-driven development with cursor/windsurf; (4) Claude Code CLI configuration, MCP servers, and Agent SDK reference; (5) n8n and Retell AI documentation. The substantive content clusters around agentic coding patterns, context management, rules-based AI guidance, and multi-agent orchestration. The document title 'astro claude websites 3x faster' does not reflect actual content.
operating_rules: Set explicit AI rules (Cascade Memories) to avoid analysis overhead on each request
Specify tech stack upfront to prevent AI from switching technologies mid-fix
Never use mock/stub data in dev/prod environments, only test
Keep context window aware: track conversation length, start new chats when context becomes bloated
Use narrow, incremental requests to agents (fix one thing at a time, test, then next)
Avoid file-size bloat: refactor when files exceed 200-300 lines
Multi-file editing requires approval on changes, but can be reviewed in parallel
Prefer simple solutions and check for code duplication before adding new functionality
Maintain separation of dev/test/prod environments explicitly in rules
For reasoning models, prompt differently than non-reasoning models (chain-of-thought style)
Start with flagship models (gpt-5, gpt-4.1), descend to faster variants only if needed
Use structured outputs and type-safety to constrain LLM outputs in production
Commit often and use rollback/checkpoint features to recover from bad iterations
Close unrelated files in editor to maximize AI productivity and context clarity
gates: Agentic behavior support: verify model supports function calling and tool calling well before using with agents
Context window saturation: monitor total tokens in conversation; trigger new chat when degradation observed
Technology stack validation: rules must explicitly lock stack to prevent AI substitution
File safety gates: avoid files over 200-300 lines; refactor to prevent bloated contexts
Mock data detection: scan all code for stub/mock patterns in non-test environments
Environment separation: verify dev/test/prod isolation before committing
Rollback point validation: ensure git and checkpoint history are available before major changes
prompts: Write a spec for an application that will be [describe]. Be as specific as possible. Include technical specification, how it operates, database schema, API endpoints.
Analyze package.json and determine our tech stack and versions, then add to rules to prevent confusion.
Is this [directory/file] dead code or still in use somewhere? Check before removing.
Run pnpm lint and fix all type errors. You can modify multiple files.
Enforce a maximum [feature] length. Make sure we don't already have code for this. Test for this after implementation.
Find all TODO comments and create a summary.
Rename the git branch to '[name]'. Show me the correct terminal command first.
Explain this code section. / Refactor this code to be faster and more efficient. / Add a docstring to this function.
Build this application based on this spec. [paste full spec].
Continue. [when adding next feature based on existing pattern]
content_ideas: Cascade Memories: system prompt + context layer that persists across chat sessions to prevent re-analysis
Multi-file editing with live approval: allows AI to fix issues across files while human reviews in parallel
In-line commands: selective code modification without touching unrelated sections
Supercomplete: multi-line autocomplete with awareness of related open files
Codelenses: single-click actions to explain, refactor, add docstrings, or fix comments
Rules system: project-level and workspace-level guardrails to lock tech choices and prevent substitution
Context-window-aware iteration: start new chats to avoid bloat; move relevant context to next chat
Vibe coding: async agent-driven development where AI writes entire features end-to-end
Structured outputs: JSON schema constraints for reliable LLM outputs in production
Reasoning vs non-reasoning model selection: reasoning for complex tasks (planning, math, code generation), non-reasoning for fast chat-like interactions
RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation): pull contextual knowledge from knowledge base to ground LLM responses
Function calling: define custom functions for agents to call; execution happens on user side (custom) or infrastructure side (built-in)
Agent orchestration: multiple agents with different tools/instructions working together; routing agent dispatches to task-specific agents
MCP (Model Context Protocol): standardized way to add external tools and integrations to agents
Tool execution modes: manual approval, auto-execute (YOLO), or intelligent (auto for safe, ask for risky)
End-to-end testing preferred over unit tests: verify full user workflow rather than isolated functions
contradictions: CONTEXT SIZING: Seg 101 says give 'as much context as possible' but also warns 'if you give it too much context it starts performing poorly' - the inflection point is experience-dependent and not specified
REFACTORING GATES: Rules say 'avoid major architecture changes after feature is working well' but also 'refactor files over 200-300 lines' - when does one override the other?
MOCK DATA POLICY: Strict prohibition on mock data in dev/prod, but OpenAI RAG docs show mock data as acceptable for testing RAG pipelines in development
MODEL SELECTION: Reasoning models recommended for 'complex tasks like code generation' but also noted as 'slower and more expensive'; no clear guidance on when speedup justifies cost tradeoff
STACK STABILITY: Rules lock tech stack to prevent switching, but also allow 'use RAG/fine-tuning/new patterns' if existing tech doesn't work - no escalation path defined
HUMAN APPROVAL: Multi-file editing requires approval on changes, but YOLO mode auto-executes everything including GitHub pushes and production deploys
weird_gold: Windsurf can highlight specific UI elements in browser preview and send only that element's code to AI context - reduces noise vs sending entire file
Typing 'continue' into Cascade with related files open is enough prompt to generate entire feature continuation - contextual awareness + pattern matching from open files
Cursor 'codelenses' offer single-click actions (explain/refactor/docstring) that generate fixes inline without chat context - UI micro-tool pattern
Git branch history + checkpoint rollback inside IDE means every AI iteration is version-controlled without manual commit discipline
Vibe coder built entire Twitter clone end-to-end via single spec paste + agentic iteration; took 100-150 hours of wall-clock time but claimed dramatic speedup over manual
MCP servers abstract away API complexity - one line of config gives LLM access to external systems; headersHelper pattern allows dynamic auth header injection at connection time
OpenAI Agents SDK uses 'sessions' with automatic conversation history management - stateful by default, eliminating manual state tracking on user side
Managed vector stores in file search tool bypass entire RAG pipeline complexity (chunking/embedding/reranking) - infrastructure handles preprocessing
Function calling parameter extraction happens inside LLM thinking - parameters extracted from conversation flow, not from explicit schema in prompt
Computer use API requires screenshot-based feedback loop (unlike other built-in tools) - action sent as parameters, user executes and sends screenshot back
Rules file format is plain markdown with code examples - parsed as system prompt context, not strict schema, allowing natural language enforcement
